verdict.root_cause: adservice is in a container crash loop and is therefore not accepting connections, and the frontend's outbound GetAds RPCs fail at the transport layer as a result. A platform-automation change lowered ad-service's container memory limit to 256m at 16:19:54Z (tr_8288272dd0bf); adservice's logs show normal ad-request serving up to ~16:14:20 and then, from 16:20:10 onward, nothing but repeated JVM/OTel-agent bootstrap sequences on a roughly 60-second cadence with no gRPC serving activity — at least eleven restarts between 16:20 and 16:27 (tr_2ba33258cf6e). The process is being killed for exceeding its (newly reduced) memory ceiling before or shortly after it reaches the serving stage, which is why adservice emits no call-count series at all for the window, neither error nor total (tr_d575d870c184). Upstream, frontend logs gRPC status 14 UNAVAILABLE with a 'no connection established' detail recurring 16:20–16:26 (tr_1cfa39c19ffd), and traces localise every error-marked span to the frontend HTTP GET -> frontend gRPC GetAds path, with the checkout subtree and all shared backends fast and clean (tr_ecdb2f0db1da). The two failure shapes on the ad path — ~2.5s calls hitting a client timeout ceiling and sub-millisecond fast failures — match a peer that is alternately unreachable during restart and refusing connections outright. Frontend's own error rate is intermittent and peaks near 10.3% because only ad-bearing pages fail (tr_c43cc564ad33), and no frontend change is recorded in the window (tr_55ed7a4f3bb9). The failing mechanism is the adservice process exhausting its available memory and being terminated, not a wrong address, credential or artifact.
verdict.reasoning: Three independent lines converge on adservice as the failing component. Traces (tr_ecdb2f0db1da) put every error span on the frontend->GetAds path and explicitly clear checkoutservice, its onward dependencies, and the shared backends, which rules out the fan-out explanations the past cart incidents warn about. Frontend logs (tr_1cfa39c19ffd) show the failure is transport-level — code 14 with no connection established, not a deadline or a quota rejection — meaning the peer was not there to answer, which is what a restart loop looks like from the caller's side. adservice logs (tr_2ba33258cf6e) confirm the peer is not there: eleven-plus JVM bootstraps between 16:20 and 16:27 with no serving lines. The empty adservice metric series (tr_d575d870c184) is consistent with a process that never lives long enough to record or export call counts. The change record (tr_8288272dd0bf) supplies the trigger — a memory limit reduced to 256m at 16:19:54, ~16 seconds before the first observed bootstrap in the crash loop — but the trigger is not the class. Per the taxonomy, a limit lowered until the process is killed for exceeding it is resource_exhaustion: the value is not naming a wrong address or artifact, it is denying the process memory it needs, and what is happening now is a JVM dying for lack of heap/native memory. The remediation that actually resolves it is restoring the prior memory limit on ad-service, i.e. reverting that configuration change; a plain restart would only re-enter the loop. Confidence is medium rather than high because no OOMKill record, exit code 137, or OutOfMemoryError line was observed — the crash cause is inferred from tight timing correlation plus the absence of any other change or error signature, and the log result was truncated across exactly the interval (16:14:20–16:20:10) where the transition occurred.
open_questions: No direct kill evidence: the adservice logs returned contain no OOMError, GC pressure, or exit-code/OOMKilled record (tr_2ba33258cf6e). Container-level restart reasons or kubelet events are needed to confirm memory as the kill cause rather than, say, a startup probe failure or the agent failing under the new limit.

The prior memory limit value is unrecorded (tr_8288272dd0bf), so the magnitude of the reduction — and whether 256m is merely tight or grossly insufficient for this JVM plus OTel javaagent — is unknown.
The 16:14:20–16:20:10 interval was truncated out of the adservice log result, so the exact onset and the first failure mode before the loop stabilised are unobserved.
All queries end at 16:28:45; nothing is known about 16:28:45–16:35, including whether the crash loop persisted, self-resolved, or was remediated.

The planner's multi-service dispatches failed, so cartservice, checkoutservice, productcatalogservice and recommendationservice were never directly examined. They are cleared only indirectly by trace sampling (tr_ecdb2f0db1da), and triage reported 7 services in blast radius plus one unmeasured edge — collateral damage or a second concurrent fault on an unexamined service cannot be excluded.

The fast-failing sub-millisecond GetAds spans versus the ~2.5s timeout spans (tr_ecdb2f0db1da) were not reconciled against the restart cadence; whether the fast failures are connection-refused during a down phase or something else on the ad path is unconfirmed.
Whether the platform-automation policy that lowered the limit will re-apply it after a manual revert, causing recurrence, is unknown.
